transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because... I guess ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, things have just been catching up with me. 

I mean, I'm holding it together at work fine, but at home and with my coursework, I'm just... a lot more wound up and short with people than I'm used to being. And I've kind of stopped doing the things that usually keep my head clear. I've been skipping out on fishing, my woodworking projects, even the first-aid workshops I usually go to. I just haven't been myself lately, so I figured I should come in.
Besides feeling wound up and irritable, have you also been feeling down, sad, or hopeless since your father-in-law moved in?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or... hopeless. It's really just the frustration and feeling on edge all the time. I don't feel down in the dumps or anything like that, just really stressed out by the whole situation.
How long ago did your father-in-law move in with you, and about how long after that did you start noticing these feelings of being wound up and on edge?

He moved in about four months ago. And as for when I started feeling this way... I'd say I noticed the strain starting within the first couple of months. It was really once the new home routines and all the day-to-day caregiving demands settled in that I started feeling so wound up.
Aside from the stress of your father-in-law's care, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things—like work, finances, or health—and having a hard time controlling that worry?

No, not really. I mean, work is fine. I don't really stress about finances or my health or anything like that. It's pretty much just tied to the situation at home. When I'm on shift, I'm focused, and I don't find myself worrying about all that other stuff. It's really just the new dynamic with him living with us that's got me so wound up.
When you feel wound up because of the situation at home, do you also notice physical signs of anxiety—like your heart racing, muscle tension, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart isn't racing or anything. I guess my shoulders might be a little tight from the stress, but I'm not restless or pacing around. It's more of a mental frustration than a physical thing.
When you describe feeling 'wound up,' would you say you mostly feel nervous or fearful, or is it more that you feel irritable and angry without an underlying sense of nervousness?

I wouldn't say I feel fearful or nervous. It's definitely more on the irritable side. I just feel... short-tempered, I guess. Like I have less patience than usual, and I get angry more easily. But no, I don't feel scared or nervous about anything.
Has this irritability led you to act out in ways that are unusual for you—like snapping at people, breaking things, or acting aggressively—rather than just feeling tense inside?

No, nothing extreme like that. I definitely haven't broken anything or gotten aggressive. I mean... I might snap at my wife over something small, which isn't really like me, but it doesn't go beyond just a quick, sharp comment. I'm definitely not throwing things or yelling at people. It's mostly just me feeling annoyed and tense on the inside.
When you think about the ongoing situation with your father-in-law's care, do you ever feel a sense of worry or apprehension about how things will go, even if it's mixed in with the irritability?

No, I don't think I'd call it worry or apprehension. It's not like I'm sitting around dreading what's going to happen next. It's just... the day-to-day reality of it is frustrating. I know what needs to be done, and it's just a lot to handle. So, no, I'm not really worried about how things will go, just annoyed with how they are right now.
